entities.name: cross-validation
entities.summary: Cross-validation is a technique used in machine learning to evaluate model performance and tune hyperparameters. It involves splitting the dataset into k folds, training the model on k-1 folds, and validating on the remaining fold. This process is repeated k times, with each fold serving as the validation set once. The average performance metric across all folds is calculated to provide a more accurate estimate of the model's true performance. Cross-validation helps avoid overfitting and is useful for hyperparameter tuning by comparing different models and selecting the best hyperparameters. Variations include k-fold, leave-one-out, stratified, and nested cross-validation, each suited to different dataset sizes and modeling goals.
